core_obligations: Reduce, via Proposition labelled proposition-check-h, to the cartesian property for an almost blow up square with X affine, and perform the Zariski descent step over an open cover with double overlaps (proof lines 11521-11558).

Handle the case where b is a closed immersion and Z is locally principal, and show with Lemma labelled lemma-almost-blow-up-unique that the fibre product condition is independent of the chosen almost blow up square (proof lines 11560-11582).

Prove the induction on the number r of generators: the case r <= 2 via Example labelled example-two-generators and assumption (4), and the induction step via the square for Z_1 = Spec(A/(f_1,f_2)), the base changed squares (I) and (II) of Lemma labelled lemma-base-change-almost-blow-up, and the induction hypothesis applied to Y and Z_1 (proof lines 11584-11689).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the affine almost blowup square and descend along a Zariski cover (proof lines 11521-11558).
Settle the case of a closed immersion and show independence of the chosen square (proof lines 11560-11582).
Induction on the number of generators, base case r <= 2 (proof lines 11584-11590).
Induction step with the auxiliary square for Z_1 and the base changes (I) and (II) (proof lines 11592-11689).
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises sheaves on one of the big h sites (Sch/S)_h: a presheaf F is a sheaf if and only if it is a Zariski sheaf, F(Y) is the equalizer of F(X) => F(X x_Y X) for every surjective flat proper finitely presented f : X -> Y with Y affine, and F turns the two almost blowup squares of Example labelled example-one-generator and Example labelled example-two-generators into cartesian diagrams of sets (statement lines 11500-11519). By Proposition labelled proposition-check-h it suffices to show the cartesian property for an almost blow up square with X affine (proof lines 11521-11528), and the proof opens with a Zariski descent reduction: if the cartesian property holds on the members U_i of an open cover and on the double overlaps U_{ijk}, it holds for the square on X (proof lines 11530-11558). The core is an induction on the number r of generators of the ideal defining Z. For r <= 2 the square may be chosen as in Example labelled example-two-generators, so assumption (4) applies (proof lines 11584-11590); for the induction step one takes Z_1 = Spec(A/(f_1,f_2)) with its almost blow up square from Example labelled example-two-generators, uses Lemma labelled lemma-base-change-almost-blow-up to obtain the two almost blow up squares (I) and (II) whose ideals are generated by fewer elements, applies the induction hypothesis to Y and Z_1, and glues the three fibre product descriptions through assumption (4) (proof lines 11592-11689). The argument also isolates a preliminary reduction that decides when b is a closed immersion and Z locally principal, and uses Lemma labelled lemma-almost-blow-up-unique to show that the truth of the fibre product condition is independent of the chosen almost blow up square (proof lines 11560-11582). The proof concludes by omitting the routine verification that the constructed s maps to s' and t, with the hint to use uniqueness of s and work affine locally (proof lines 11690-11693). Building the induction on the number of generators so that both assumptions (3) and (4) apply after base change is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
